entries.section: (1) The opening greeting

paragraphs.text: The content of Paul's letter is evident from the apostolic greeting at the beginning of his epistles. As he addresses the Thessalonians, who were suffering persecution from the unbelieving Jews, he shows his love and humility, and does not call himself an Apostle, since this was already known to them.

He joins with himself his two disciples, Silvanus (Silas) and Timothy, in sending the greeting to them, although he alone is the writer of the letter, for those who are afflicted need the sympathy of many.

He shows the fatherhood of God when he says "God our Father," so that they might feel His care for them, and likewise Christ the Savior, who unites the believers, Gentiles and Jews, in one Church. And he sends them the grace of God, which is able to give them an inner peace that the outward afflictions they suffer cannot take away.

If St. Paul writes to the Thessalonians, who suffered persecution from unbelievers, in order to encourage them with grace and peace, then may you take care to encourage everyone who is in distress or suffering, whether a small child or a grown person, because your fatherly care and encouragement inspire him to bear sufferings with patience and courage, and you yourself are filled with it, so that you too are strengthened by the grace of God.

entries.section: (2) Thanksgiving to God for their faith, love and hope

paragraphs.text: The Apostle encourages them to endure sufferings by praising their virtues, saying: we give thanks to God for the fruits of grace that abound in you, for God is the source of all goodness in men.
It was the Apostle's custom to spend long hours in prayer for the Churches, and for the particular need of each Church.

Perhaps we turn to the Lord to pray for our brethren in circumstances of grief, danger and sickness, but it is beautiful to return to Him with thanksgiving for His grace in those who are being saved, and also to pray if they suffer from the weakness of their spiritual condition.

entries.section: (2) Thanksgiving to God for their faith, love and hope

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle mentions the three virtues that are the fruit of the work of grace in them, but he does not speak here of the virtues themselves, but of their results, namely the work of faith, the labor of love, the patience of hope. Work of your faith: that is, fruitful, active and effective faith, by which the reality of our faith is shown before God, "for faith without works is dead" (Jas 2:26). Labor of your love: true love is a sacrificial love, which labors for the sake of others and in the service of the brethren.

Patience of your hope: hope grants consolation in sorrow and gives patience in affliction, and the Lord Jesus, to Him be the glory, is Himself the hope who gives the strength to endure, and He is also the example in patience.

entries.section: (2) Thanksgiving to God for their faith, love and hope

paragraphs.text: St. Paul knew that the fruit of the Spirit which appeared in their lives was the proof of the new life that is in Christ, and so they had become chosen according to the foreknowledge of God, and had become a people set apart and consecrated by God to be the object of His love. On this basis St. Paul sets aside the Jews' idea that they are the chosen people, to put in its place the spiritual election of those who believe in Christ (Gal 6:16), and also to give them encouragement, as he affirms God's election of them.

entries.section: (3) Their faith an example to others

paragraphs.text: What manner of men: how greatly Paul and his disciples bore the labors of the ministry, in spiritual manliness and with much self-sacrifice.
For your sake: to win your souls.

Paul makes clear that his preaching of the Gospel in Thessalonica was not in word only, but he delivered it to them in confidence and faith and in the power of the Holy Spirit working in him, and he endured afflictions and labor in preaching in order to draw their souls to Christ.

entries.section: (3) Their faith an example to others

paragraphs.text: The life of Paul and his companions, with self-denial and holy conduct, left a deep impression on the souls of the Thessalonians, so they imitated them. They received the word in much affliction and suffered bitter persecution, yet they were joyful in the message that told them of the forgiveness of their sins and the hope of eternal life. The saying applied to them: "as sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing" (2 Cor 6:10).

entries.section: (3) Their faith an example to others

paragraphs.text: Macedonia: the northern part of Greece.
Achaia: the southern part of Greece.

The change in their lives was so great that others quickly noticed it, and they became "ensamples" to all who were in Macedonia and who received the faith as they did in the north, and also in Achaia in the south. Their lives bore witness that they were in a living relationship with God, and they were true lights in the darkness of the world.

entries.section: (3) Their faith an example to others

paragraphs.text: The believers in Thessalonica were a living witness to the power of life with Christ, so their report sounded forth like a trumpet not only in Macedonia and Achaia but also in every direction, and this not because of miracles they performed but because of their faith in God. Thessalonica was an important commercial center, so the news spread from that center to every place. And before the greatness of their faith, Paul found no words with which to glorify their faith, because it had become plain to all.

entries.section: (3) Their faith an example to others

paragraphs.text: When St. Paul preached in the various lands of Greece, he found them marveling at the Thessalonians' acceptance of his message and their turning from the worship of idols to the worship of God; indeed, they hastened to tell St. Paul of this, which helped the other lands to receive the faith and to stand firm in Christ.

entries.section: (3) Their faith an example to others

paragraphs.text: The Thessalonians await the Second Coming of the Lord, which is the hope of all Christianity and by which the divine promises are fulfilled in eternal life. For the One whom they await is the very One who died for them, and we await Him as Savior, after He reconciled us with God the Father by the Cross, to change the form of the body of our humility so that it may be in the likeness of the body of His glory (Phil 3:21). This too is a new encouragement that every suffering is followed by great glory, as happened to our Lord Jesus Christ, who bore the sufferings of salvation and then sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

Know, my brother, that your enduring of the faith with thanksgiving, and your holding fast to your principles in spite of afflictions, not only brings an abundance of God's blessings upon you but also influences those around you more than any words.
Paul's fatherhood and longings

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: For you yourselves, brethren, know that our coming among you was not in vain, not only because our coming among you, we the servants of Christ, had a great effect at that time, but also because our work was afterward shown to be firm, deeply rooted and successful, for the fruits continued and increased.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: The bodily sufferings that befell us in Philippi, such as beating, imprisonment and the tearing of garments, and the moral sufferings of contempt and scorn, did not keep us from coming to you and boldly proclaiming the Gospel, whatever persecution we met, for the faithful servants of Christ do not draw back, because they count themselves unworthy to be dishonored for His name's sake.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: For our preaching is not falsehood but assured truth, nor is it from an impure mind aiming at selfish ends, nor in craftiness to hide something for a purpose of one's own, but with all frankness and plainness.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: For God chose us by His grace and entrusted us with preaching in His name, with all that this includes of the highest degrees of responsibility, so we serve to please God and not to please men at the expense of the pleasure of God, who searches the hearts and tests the thoughts.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: You yourselves bear witness that we did not use words such as the flattery of men requires when they have some purpose of their own, and we did not speak smooth words or gentle phrases out of greed and love of money and desire for shameful gain. And while the Thessalonians can bear witness to all this concerning his outward conduct, there is another witness to the inner thought, known to God, who knows the secrets of hearts.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: Dignity as apostles of Christ: St. Paul toiled and worked with his own hands to meet his personal needs, although he was not bound to do so and it was his right that they should provide for his needs, like the rest of Christ's disciples who preach in the various lands.

True servants of God do not seek their own glory, but hide themselves so as to show Christ, as John the Baptist said, "He must increase, but I must decrease" (Jn 3:30). The Apostle did not use his apostolic authority except where it was necessary, and he sought nothing to please himself, but his only aim was the glory of God.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: Paul shows that he and his disciples were gentle and tender, and with all meekness, humility and love they sat in the midst of their brethren in full familiarity, as a nursing mother sits with her little ones around her, holding them to her breast in tenderness.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: Thus they treated them with all tenderness and love, giving every effort for their edification in Christ, giving them not only the Gospel of God but their own selves also, for they were ready to lay down their lives for them as Christ did for us all, all this out of their love for them.

entries.section: (1) Preaching without compensation

paragraphs.text: The Apostle reminds them of the striving and sufferings they bore for the sake of their edification, and during their preaching they worked with their hands to meet their needs without burdening them. The Apostle offered the Gospel freely so that there might be no blemish on the ministry, although it was his right to live of the Gospel because he proclaimed the Gospel. Paul worked at the trade of tent-making.
The Apostle also makes clear that ministry is not merely teaching, but also upbringing, with every follow-up and effort, so that the one served may reach spiritual success.

If you are a servant, a father or a mother, may you be tender toward those you serve and ready to lay down your life for them as Christ did with you. Look at His body given for you on the altar every day, so that you may be eager to sacrifice for those you serve, knowing that they need your love as nursing infants need the one who brings them up, and trust that God's reward to you is great and the tenderness He will pour out upon you exceeds all your expectations.

entries.section: (2) His fatherhood and purity in ministry

paragraphs.text: Men can judge only the outward conduct, so besides asking for their witness to his conduct, he also calls God to witness for him. For the righteous man is not merely one who does works of righteousness, but one who does works of righteousness in a mind befitting a righteous man. Here the Apostle enumerates the aspects of his conduct, which are:
Holily: that is, purity.
Justly: that is, upright conduct.
Unblameably: that is, without anyone reproving him for a fault he commits.

entries.section: (2) His fatherhood and purity in ministry

paragraphs.text: As you saw how we offered our spiritual exhortation to each one of you with all sincerity, as a father counsels his children, and we encouraged you to walk worthy of God and worthy of the calling to which you were called.

entries.section: (2) His fatherhood and purity in ministry

paragraphs.text: Charged: here this means the aspect of warning and admonition.

When the Thessalonians worshiped idols, they walked as befits idols, but when they returned to the true God, their walk became as befits God, who accomplished salvation for them through His Son and opened to them the gates of eternal glory in His Kingdom.

Thus the warmth of the Apostle's heart is made plain, as he follows each one individually with real concern like a father with his children, and after showing them his fatherhood, he calls them to upright Christian conduct, and so the servant should be.

Do not seek your own interest or comfort when you serve God, whether in your care for your children or in your service in the Church. Be pure in your words and thoughts so that you may be pleasing before God and not cause those you serve or bring up to stumble. Care for every individual and show him your love, so that he is not lost in the crowd but is strengthened, however weak he may be.

entries.section: (3) Enduring persecutions

paragraphs.text: After St. Paul spoke about himself and his disciples in verses (1-12), he turns to speak about the Thessalonians in verses (13, 14). The Apostle begins by giving thanks to God for the Thessalonians' entering into the faith. In this he teaches us always to give the credit to God, who crowns our works with success, and not to ourselves, and that thanksgiving should always be in our lives. The Thessalonians received the word not as the word of men, that is, of Paul, Silas and Timothy, but as the word of God, with all reverence, awe and faith.
Through Paul and his disciples they heard the voice of God Himself and His message calling them to eternal life, and the word of God working in them, cleansing and purifying them.

Studying the word of God reveals to us our spiritual condition, so if we are diligent and persistent in studying it, our lives will be pure and pleasing to the Lord. May we take care each day to read a portion of the Holy Bible and choose a verse to apply in our lives, so that it will reveal some of our faults and direct us in the path of spiritual growth.

entries.section: (3) Enduring persecutions

paragraphs.text: In Christ Jesus: an expression St. Paul uses in many of his epistles, by which he means union and fellowship with Christ, like the union of the head with the members of the body, which is His Church. You have suffered from the Gentiles around you who rejected the faith, just as the Church of Jerusalem also suffered from the Jews who did not believe. The Christian, whether of Jewish or Gentile origin, is persecuted, because Satan is against him and stirs up the wicked against him. Here we see also the unity of sufferings, just as there is also the unity of fruits and reward. Thus it is clear that there is no preaching or faith without suffering, so that no one should be troubled.

entries.section: (3) Enduring persecutions

paragraphs.text: The Jews seized Christ and handed Him over to the Gentile Romans, who killed Him, so they were considered the killers; and likewise they killed their prophets, as the Lord Christ said of them, "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee..." (Mt 23:37). And now they persecute us, the Apostles, and do not care to please God, although they pretend that this is their task and calling. They are enemies of all mankind, for God distinguished them from the Gentiles who worship idols by making them a special people for Himself, to be an example to the rest of the peoples and to draw them to the faith; but on the contrary they killed the prophets and Christ Himself and became a bad example, so they hid the light of God from the world and in this became opposed to it, and in their pride they despised the other peoples and races.

entries.section: (3) Enduring persecutions

paragraphs.text: The Jews do not want the salvation of the Gentiles, but despise them and regard them as dogs, and do not want the message of salvation and their share in the Messiah to reach them, and want eternal destruction to come upon all the Gentiles. This is the secret of their hatred toward Paul, because he proclaimed Jesus Christ to the pagans, saying that God is the God of the Jews and the Gentiles. They killed the prophets, then the Lord Jesus, and persecuted the Apostles, and so on until they fill up the measure of their evil, as was their way in ancient times. But God turned their persecution of the Apostles and their refusal of the message into the directing of the Gospel to the Gentiles who accepted the faith, so evil was turned into good by the providential work of God. But the Jews, because of the blood of the prophets which stains their life and history, and especially because of the blood of Christ, brought upon themselves the guilt of blood, and so the wrath of God came upon them. This appeared in the Romans' persecution of them until they destroyed Jerusalem in the year 70 AD, and persecutions continued to overtake them.

Enduring sufferings is difficult, but it is a proof of our sonship to God, because it is a fellowship in His sufferings and a declaration of our love for Him. May we accept with thanksgiving the afflictions that come upon us, on condition that we are not at fault in anything.

entries.section: (4) His longing for them

paragraphs.text: In this verse we meet the overflowing love expressed in the abundant emotions of St. Paul, as he speaks of his intense longing for them and his urgent desire to see them, after being absent from them from the time he was with them until he wrote this letter to them, a period of about four months; but his absence from them was in body while their hearts remained bound together, for he remembered them without ceasing in his prayers.

entries.section: (4) His longing for them

paragraphs.text: He strove with all sincere desire to find a way to come to them and see them, and he tried this more than once, but Satan hindered him from coming to them through the opposing Jews. Here a question arises: can Satan hinder the work of the Lord and His servants? The answer is yes. He stirs up persecution against them and obstructs them.
The second question: does Satan act as he pleases? The answer: no, for he works within the limits that the Lord permits him, so Satan's success in anything also depends on the will of God.

entries.section: (4) His longing for them

paragraphs.text: The Apostle shows the place of the Thessalonians in his heart, and declares to them that his service to them is what gives him the crown and the glory in the day of judgment and joy before Christ our Lord.

Take care to express your feelings of love for others so as to overcome the thoughts of doubt or faint-heartedness that may fight against them. All people need encouragement, especially since Satan continually creates misunderstanding in various forms, so we must overcome him by showing continual love to all who are around us. The sending of Timothy and his comforting Paul with news of them

entries.section: (1) The sending of Timothy to them

paragraphs.text: Paul had an intense longing to be reassured about the Thessalonians, and since he was unable to come to them himself because of the Jews' opposition, he preferred that he and Silas alone remain in Athens, and he sent the disciple dearest to his heart, Timothy, to Thessalonica, and in humility calls him "our brother, and minister of God, and our fellowlabourer," to complete their evangelization and exhortation so that they might stand firm in the faith.

entries.section: (1) The sending of Timothy to them

paragraphs.text: Appointed thereunto: the Apostles, together with the rest of the believers, are exposed to persecutions that test them and prove them.

The Apostle feared that some of them might lack depth of faith and forsake Christ because of the Jews' persecution of them, for he had already told them that affliction and persecution are not strange in the life of the Christian, because they are a test of his faith.

entries.section: (1) The sending of Timothy to them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul reminds them that when he was with them before this time, he told them that storms of persecution must break upon them and upon him also in the city of Thessalonica, and this indeed happened, and all the believers there knew of it, and because of it he was compelled to leave Thessalonica and go to Berea (Acts 17:5-10).

Let us be strong when sufferings meet us, and let us not doubt the love of God the Father because of sorrows and hard circumstances, for He permits them for our edification: they give us spiritual firmness, free us from all negligence, make us feel for our afflicted brethren, and urge us to cling to Him and lean on Him, so that we grow deeper spiritually.

entries.section: (1) The sending of Timothy to them

paragraphs.text: When I could no longer forbear: I could not bear patiently the lack of news from you and my fear for you, that you might be shaken by the Jews' persecution of you.

Because I knew with certainty that temptation must come upon you, I sent to you to learn whether our preaching was still alive in you, and to be sure that you were still standing firm in the faith and that the fruit of our labor had not been lost.

entries.section: (2) Their news gladdens his heart

paragraphs.text: When Timothy returned from Thessalonica, he brought Paul good tidings of the steadfastness of their faith, the abundance of their love, their constant remembrance of him and their longing to see him, just as Paul too had a great longing to see them and always remembered them in his thought. So we notice the prayers and the feelings of mutual love between the two sides.

entries.section: (2) Their news gladdens his heart

paragraphs.text: Our necessity: necessary needs that he does not obtain, that is, he suffers in obtaining the barest necessities such as food or rest.

Your faith and your sincerity overflowed in us with comfort and joy in spite of all the difficulties we pass through. The Apostle was surrounded by outward circumstances of sorrow, but in his heart there was joy because he was reassured about the believers.

entries.section: (2) Their news gladdens his heart

paragraphs.text: Paul had feared that the faith of the Thessalonians would be shaken, but when Timothy came and told him of the steadfastness of their faith, this news refreshed Paul's heart as if life had returned to him, that is, he enjoyed rest and joy.

entries.section: (2) Their news gladdens his heart

paragraphs.text: The Apostle feels that any thanks he offers to God is little and not proportionate to His grace and to the joy with which He compensated him when he heard of the steadfastness of the faith of the Thessalonians. Here Paul's joy at the success of his ministry is seen to be greater than his concern for his personal comfort, for the true servant rejoices in the success of his ministry more than in anything, and the sign of that is the steadfastness of those he serves in the Lord and not their attachment to his own person.

Give thanks to God for all His gifts, and for the faith and rest of those around you, and for every work He brings to success through your hands, because thanksgiving gladdens your heart and strengthens you and others in the faith.

entries.section: (3) His wishes to see them and for their growth

paragraphs.text: St. Paul was not seeking bodily rest, but worked and struggled night and day in prayers for the Thessalonians. Preaching, for him, was not merely sermons and holding meetings; rather, he always carried in his mind those who had believed and hoped to return to them to complete their evangelization, that is, what was lacking of his teaching to them, in order to establish their faith.

entries.section: (3) His wishes to see them and for their growth

paragraphs.text: God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ: here is a clear witness to the unity of the Father and the Son.
The Apostle did not say that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ direct (in the dual) our way, because the Father and the Son are one in the divine essence.
Direct our way unto you: make our arrival at Thessalonica easy, and guide us and support us in completing your evangelization and ministry.
Paul asks that God help him to reach Thessalonica and complete his ministry there.

entries.section: (3) His wishes to see them and for their growth

paragraphs.text: The Apostle says: whether I come to you or am unable to come, God is able to increase your love for one another in the Church of Thessalonica and toward all men, even as we also love you with great love.

entries.section: (3) His wishes to see them and for their growth

paragraphs.text: Establishing in holiness is a continuing process, that is, we grow in holiness until Christ comes in His Second Coming, full of glory with all His saints, and we stand before the judgment seat of Christ where we are found blameless, a glorious Church, holy and without blemish.

May you be ambitious for spiritual growth, so that you long for your prayers and your knowledge of the Holy Bible to increase, and your love and your service to others to increase also, so that you experience each day what is new in the love of God. Holiness, love and the resurrection

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: St. Paul calls the believers in Thessalonica to hold fast to the Christian conduct that pleases God, and even to grow in it.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: St. Paul reminds them of the earlier teachings they received from him, which guide them to the way of holiness. It is beautiful of the Apostle to put "the Lord Jesus" in everything: in (v. 1) he says "we beseech you ... by the Lord Jesus," and here he says "what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus." For when Christ is the goal, all our actions are in the right direction, not merely carrying out commandments but being careful to please God and working to increase, that is, spiritual growth, until we reach holiness.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: God has set us apart from the world and sanctified us and dedicated us to Himself. For the sake of this holiness he calls them to reject fornication, which was bound up with the idolatrous worship out of which these Thessalonians had come, for the lust of the flesh was part of their former religion.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: His vessel: his wife.

The Apostle speaks here of purity in the relationship between husband and wife, as he said in (Heb 13:4), so that a person does not apply the lusts and perversions of the world within his marital relationship, but feels the presence of Christ with him in this relationship, so that it is an expression of love, and he considers the feelings of the other and keeps away from any perversion practiced by the people of the world.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: Not knowing God is the fountain of impurity. Because the pagan Gentiles do not know the happiness of life with God, sexual passions are their paradise, and they understand nothing of marriage but passion and lust with all their perversions, to fill the emptiness of their hearts.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: The Apostle affirms the teaching he had already given, which is that no one should go beyond and covet the wives of others or any unmarried woman, a matter that is a grave violation of the commandment of the Lord Christ in (Mt 5:27, 28), for God avenges those who regard fornication as permissible.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: In view of the holy calling with which we were called, we must live in holiness and keep away from these things, not only because we fear God's vengeance and discipline, but because our life is purity and holiness.

entries.section: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

paragraphs.text: He who despises the commandment does not dishonor only his own body and the body of another, but dishonors God, who gave us His Holy Spirit to give us strength and help to be holy and blameless before Him. Therefore whoever defiles his body dishonors the Holy Spirit, who sanctified his body by the sacrament of the Holy Myron.

Put Christ before you in all your steps and in your relationship with the opposite sex, and do not allow your eyes or your mind to be defiled by the evil of the world. And when you draw near to your wife, remember Christ who blesses you, so that you behave with propriety and love and consider her feelings.

entries.section: (2) Love, quietness and work

paragraphs.text: The Thessalonians needed to be written to about holiness, because they were liable to fall back into their old habits, while brotherly love was the distinguishing mark of the life of that Church and the secret of its success.

How we wish that the spirit of love would prevail in our churches today, for the weakness of the Church in any age is the result of its lack of love. Love is the fruit of the new nature given to all who are born of God and who are in constant and continual fellowship with Him, and it is very important and essential in our Christian life.

entries.section: (2) Love, quietness and work

paragraphs.text: The brethren: the believers.
Macedonia: the northern part of Greece, whose capital was Thessalonica.

The believers of Thessalonica practiced brotherly love toward all the believers in Macedonia, and the Apostle was glad of that when Timothy brought him the good news of their faith and love, but he asks them to increase more and more, for growth and increase are necessary in the Christian life, since we learn them from the commandments of Christ and His redemption of us, and they are accomplished by continual striving.

entries.section: (2) Love, quietness and work

paragraphs.text: Your own business: your responsibilities.
He also enjoins them to be quiet in dealing with others so that they may live in peace, and that each one should carry out his responsibilities and his work, so that he is not a burden to others.

entries.section: (2) Love, quietness and work

paragraphs.text: Them that are without: that is, the unbelievers.

Unbelievers keep their eyes open to watch the conduct of the believers, the members of the new religion, and likewise the rulers of the nation watch them. So walk in the way that makes them see in you a community that goes about its work in quietness and peace, and faithful citizens who fear God and work diligently to the extent that meets their needs, so that you do not stretch out your hands to anyone.

Take care to fulfill your responsibilities and do not wait until others demand them of you, but try to help others instead of demanding their help, and in this way you show your love for them in practice and become an image of Christ, who gave Himself for the world.

entries.section: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

paragraphs.text: The Apostle does not rebuke the believers for their grief at the loss of their loved ones, but comforts them, saying of them that they are "asleep," that is, sleeping, in the hope of the resurrection, so they should not grieve like the rest who believe in the annihilation of man by death.

entries.section: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

paragraphs.text: If we believe that the Lord Jesus died and raised Himself, then the believers who have fallen asleep, and about whose fate you feel anxious, the Lord will raise up and bring with Him alive, for He is the Head and we are the members of the body, and what happens to the Head must happen to the members also.

entries.section: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

paragraphs.text: St. Paul declares the sequence of the events that will take place at the Second Coming of Christ: those who will be alive at this coming will not precede the dead, meaning that they will not be ahead in entering the Kingdom of Heaven before those who have fallen asleep.

entries.section: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

paragraphs.text: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven and command the dead to rise from the sleep of death and come forth to eternal life. The three expressions, a shout, the voice of the archangel, the trump of God, are meant to declare the greatness of Christ's Second Coming. What is meant by the resurrection from the dead here is the resurrection of the bodies, for the spirits of the dead continue to live since they departed from the body, that is, the spirit does not die, so the bodies raised from the dead are united with the spirits to stand before God the Judge, and this happens first, that is, the living do not enter the Kingdom before those who have fallen asleep, but those who have fallen asleep rise and all enter together at one time.

entries.section: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

paragraphs.text: Caught up: the believers in Christ will be caught up, that is, lifted up to heaven to meet Christ, and He will bring them into His Kingdom. The rapture takes place on the day of judgment, at the moment of entering the Kingdom, and not before this, as some sects believe.

As for those who will be alive at the Second Coming, they will be taken quickly, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, to meet Christ in the heavenly glories, after their bodies are changed into the likeness of the body of Christ after His resurrection. All the laws of gravity will be cast aside, because the very power of God which raised the Lord Jesus from the dead and seated Him in glory is what will carry His saints into the air and the clouds.
Our meeting Him before He reaches the earth is a proof of our intense longing for Him and our not fearing the judgment, the fear that drives the wicked to hide from Him.

entries.section: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

paragraphs.text: The Apostle asks them to repeat these words in one another's hearing and to be comforted concerning the temporary separation from loved ones.

Eternity is not far from you, and Christ wants to lift you up with Him to the Kingdom. May you cast your sins from you and draw near to God in prayers, and not be troubled by afflictions because they are temporary, for your Christ will compensate you for all this with joys that cannot be expressed.
Christian conduct and preparation for the Second Coming

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: Some believers err in trying, by calculations, to predict the time of the Second Coming. The Apostle told them when he was with them that no one knows the time of Christ's coming, so he sees no need to repeat what he had already explained to them.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: Perfectly: with certainty.

St. Paul repeats his statement that the time of the Lord's coming is unknown and that He will come suddenly like a thief who attacks in the night. The comparison of Christ's Second Coming to a thief is mentioned eight times in the New Testament, two of them in this chapter, to urge us to spiritual watchfulness and constant vigilance.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: When the wicked people of the world are sunk in their material lusts and imagine that they are materially secure in these pleasures, their hearts suddenly fall in fear and terror at their destruction by the Second Coming of Christ, as the hour of labor comes upon a woman with child, and there will be no escape for them.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: But the believers live in the light, that is, in goodness, and expect the coming of the Lord, and this knowledge of theirs must lead them to watchfulness and vigilance; and so that day will not surprise them as it surprises the others.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: Light: an expression for the pure, good life lived by the children of God, and it is the opposite of darkness, which is a symbol of evil.
Day: an expression for the clear spiritual life, and it is the opposite of the night, which is a symbol of sin working in secret.
St. Paul affirms that all believers live a pure life and keep away from evil in preparation for the coming of Christ.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: What is meant by sleep here is not the sleep of the body, but slackness or neglect in spiritual matters, remembering always that the Second Coming of Christ must take place.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: There is no place for neglect and debauchery for those who belong to the light and to the day. The picture of night here suggests the heedlessness of one who sleeps by his own will, and likewise immersion in pleasures, especially the drinking of wine, and drunkenness also means being occupied with material things instead of God.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: The sons of the day ought to be sober. Preparation by spiritual watchfulness requires arming ourselves with spiritual weapons to repel all the attacks of the adversary, the enemy of good. Here the Apostle Paul makes use of the picture of the Roman soldier at war: faith is the breastplate that protects the chest from the arrows of the enemy, which are doubt and hatred. Likewise love protects a person from anger and from being affected by the insults of others. And the helmet protects the head, the center of thoughts, so that all thought is on heavenly things and on the awaited salvation that we hope for.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: The believers have been appointed to salvation, for we do not await wrath but the obtaining of salvation, which the Lord accomplished on the Cross in order to give it to us at His Second Coming.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: Wake: alive, striving with spiritual watchfulness.
Sleep: we have ended our life and fallen asleep.
We have obtained the merits of salvation through our Redeemer Jesus Christ, so whether we are found alive or asleep at His Second Coming, we shall all live together with Him.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: The Apostle closes this section as he closed verses (13-18) in the previous chapter, in which he also spoke of the resurrection and the Second Coming, with the same phrase, "comfort one another," for when we think of the Second Coming of Christ and the general resurrection we are comforted and comfort one another concerning those who have fallen asleep. And when we think of the day of the Lord we remind one another that God has not appointed us to wrath but to obtain salvation, so we are always joyful and comforted and strengthen one another by encouraging one another to worship and good works. This they were doing, but St. Paul wanted them to increase in it.

May we remember eternity with its comforts, joys and happiness, so that we are comforted and strengthened and advance in our spiritual life, and busy ourselves with prayers, praises, reading, meditations and works of mercy toward every person, so that we are ready to receive our heavenly Bridegroom, our Lord Jesus Christ.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Know: care for and respect.
Labour: serve in the various ministries in the Church.
Are over you: shepherd you and arrange all your needs.

Admonish you: teach you by preaching so that you keep away from evil and live with Christ. This epistle is one of the oldest writings of the New Testament, and in it St. Paul shows the importance of esteeming the shepherds of the Church, who include the bishops, the priests, the deacons and all the servants.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Esteem them very highly: esteeming the shepherds in love means:
1- Obeying them and submitting to them.
2- Providing for their needs.
3- Helping them to complete their ministry.

Be at peace among yourselves: because Satan stirs up troubles and factions and, at times, the insubordination of some, as happened in the Church of Corinth, so the Apostle here directs them to the importance of holding fast to peace in the relationships of the believers with one another within the Church.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Warn: teach firmly and direct those who err to repentance.
Unruly: those who are not subject to the Church and who walk by their own ideas.

Comfort the feebleminded: those who are greatly distressed if they fall into a great sin or their sins are repeated, so they need to be encouraged to repent and begin anew, holding fast to Christ the Savior. Support the weak: those who fall into despair before afflictions or stumble at any improper act or problem, so they need support to continue their life with God.
Be patient toward all men: all people are liable to error or negligence, so they need longsuffering and gentleness from us.

The Apostle asks them to rebuke those who depart from the faith and the order of the Church, and at the same time to encourage those who doubt themselves and the weak who despair because of their many sins and the afflictions around them, and to continue showing their love with longsuffering toward all.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Practical Christianity is to bear the evil of others, and even to do good in return for evil; for love is what makes us bear with the wicked, and by good we quench every flame of sin.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: He who makes the Lord the source of his joy can rejoice at all times, even in circumstances of sorrow. But the Christian who remains in a state of gloom and depression does not trust in the power of his God and His care and love.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: We ought to walk through life with our hearts always lifted up to God, for prayer is fellowship with God, and when we pray at all times we share God in all the steps of our life's journey.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Thanksgiving in everything flows from our knowing that all the circumstances we pass through, with their sufferings and afflictions, come to us from God. God is the One who holds the reins of affairs, and He may at times permit unpleasant things for our good: "all things work together for good to them that love God" (Rom 8:28). So if we want to fulfill the will of God on our part and gladden His heart, we must live a life of surrender and thank Him in every condition, for every condition and in every condition.

The true Christian feels for the weak and hastens to their aid and to strengthen them without irritation or contempt, because love is what moves him toward all, so he does not think of himself but of others first, and feels his spiritual fatherhood and cares for the salvation of all.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit appeared on the day of Pentecost in the form of tongues of fire, that is, a blazing flame, as a symbol of His activity and effectiveness, for He is a light that illumines the mind and a power that kindles the spirit of man. So anything that hinders the work of the Spirit in us we must guard against, and this means persisting in not repenting of sin, or slackness, negligence and preoccupation away from God.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Prophesyings: in the New Testament, prophecy means speaking about the coming Kingdom of God, that is, all the spiritual teachings and preparation for the Kingdom.
Here is a warning against despising preaching, as when we say, for example, that the preaching brought nothing new, or when we harden our hearts before the word of God.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Prove every counsel or teaching you hear: is it in agreement with the teachings of the Church, the Holy Bible and the guidance of the father of confession? If you find it good, hold fast to all that is good and reject everything else.

entries.section: (2) Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Let us abstain from every appearance of evil, or even any intention of it, however slight it may seem; for we may do something from which we mean no harm to anyone, yet it may cause another person for whom Christ died to stumble, so we must abstain from evil by doing it or even by merely intending to do it, that is, the intention of evil is counted as sin.

entries.section: (3) Prayers and greetings

paragraphs.text: Sanctify you wholly: God is able to make you dedicated to Him and to fill your hearts with peace and to be your only aim.

May your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved: God establishes your whole being, spirit, soul and body, that you may live all your life for Him and be blameless on the day of judgment before Christ. The Apostle wishes for the work of God's grace in them to consecrate their lives to Him until their end.

entries.section: (3) Prayers and greetings

paragraphs.text: God who called us is faithful and will continue His work in us and fulfill His promises, and He is the One who will keep us and perfect us until the day of the coming of the Lord: "he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ" (Phil 1:6).

entries.section: (3) Prayers and greetings

paragraphs.text: The great Apostle of the Gentiles, in spite of the station he had reached among the Churches, felt in humility his need of the prayers of the believers. He prayed for them and desires that they in turn pray for him, and in this way fellowship is realized among all the believers.

entries.section: (3) Prayers and greetings

paragraphs.text: Our greeting to one another must be holy, that is, sincere and free from hypocrisy. The Apostle here stresses sincerity when we greet one another.

entries.section: (3) Prayers and greetings

paragraphs.text: The Apostle wanted to be sure that his letter would reach every person so that all might benefit from what it contains.

entries.section: (3) Prayers and greetings

paragraphs.text: This is the form of the apostolic blessing which St. Paul uses, and this blessing contains all spiritual good and is sufficient for every need.

Take care to pray for everyone around you and for every problem you hear about, for prayer is mighty because it opens the mercies of God, who is able to do all things, and therefore also care for the prayers of others for you, for they support you in all your steps.
